statements.text: All 42 patients who underwent diagnostic testing had results concordant with their cfDNA-WG screening result.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Diagnostic testing was performed in 42 subjects (11.2%), with seven discordant results
statements.note: The abstract reports seven discordant results among the 42 subjects with diagnostic testing, including trisomy 8, four single-gene disorders and two mosaicisms.

statements.text: Among 376 pregnancies with abnormal ultrasound findings, cfDNA whole-genome screening returned an abnormal result in 6.4% of cases.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: cfDNA-WG was abnormal in 24 cases (6.4%).
statements.note: 24 of the 376 subjects (6.4%) had an abnormal cfDNA-WG result.

statements.text: Fetuses with multiple congenital anomalies had a higher rate of abnormal cfDNA-WG results than those with an isolated soft marker.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Ultrasound findings included multiple congenital anomalies (n = 123), isolated structural anomaly (n = 132), isolated soft marker (n = 63), thickened nuchal translucency (n = 50), and fetal growth restriction (n = 8).
statements.note: The abstract gives the number of subjects in each ultrasound category but does not report abnormal-result rates by category.

statements.text: Trisomy 21 was the single most common abnormal cfDNA-WG finding, accounting for 10 of the 24 abnormal results.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Trisomy 21 (n = 10), Trisomy 18 (n = 6), Trisomy 13 (n = 2), and Monosomy X (n = 3)
statements.note: The breakdown lists Trisomy 21 (n = 10) ahead of Trisomy 18 (6), Monosomy X (3), Trisomy 13 (2), one Trisomy 22 and two copy number variants.

statements.text: SOAT1 expression rose with glioma grade, and the link between high expression and worse prognosis held in multivariable Cox models.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: SOAT1 expression in gliomas increased with tumor grade. High SOAT1 expression was associated with worse prognosis, and this association remained significant in multivariable Cox models.
statements.note: Both the grade trend and the multivariable prognostic association are stated in the results.

statements.text: Pharmacological inhibition of SOAT1 slowed glioma cell growth in vitro.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: providing a foundation for future research into potential therapeutic targets and prognostic biomarkers
statements.note: The study is correlative; no drug or knockdown experiment is reported, and therapeutic targeting is mentioned only as a direction for future work.

statements.text: Glioma patients with high SOAT1 expression had lower circulating neutrophil counts and a lower neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: patients with high SOAT1 expression exhibited elevated circulating neutrophils, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR)
statements.note: The abstract reports the opposite: elevated circulating neutrophils and a higher NLR in patients with high SOAT1 expression.

statements.text: Besides TCGA and CGGA data, the study included 195 glioma patients resected at a single institution between January 2016 and December 2020.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A retrospective cohort of 195 glioma patients who underwent surgical resection at our institution between January 2016 and December 2020 was also included.
statements.note: The methods describe a retrospective institutional cohort of 195 surgically resected glioma patients from this period.

statements.text: PTGES3 drives esophageal cancer progression by maintaining telomere length.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Knockdown of PTGES3 significantly suppressed EC cell migration, invasion, and clonogenic ability, supporting its oncogenic role.
statements.note: PTGES3 was validated phenotypically (migration, invasion, clonogenicity); no telomere-length measurement or mechanism is reported.

statements.text: The prognostic risk model was built from six telomere-related genes significantly associated with survival in esophageal cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Six TRGs significantly associated with prognosis were identified to establish a risk model.
statements.note: Six prognostic TRGs were identified and used to establish the risk model.

statements.text: Silencing PTGES3 in esophageal cancer cells reduced their migration, invasion and colony-forming ability.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Knockdown of PTGES3 significantly suppressed EC cell migration, invasion, and clonogenic ability
statements.note: PTGES3 knockdown significantly suppressed migration, invasion and clonogenic ability.

statements.text: High-risk patients had lower TP53 and TTN mutation rates than low-risk patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: High-risk patients had worse survival, higher TP53 and TTN mutation rates
statements.note: The abstract states that high-risk patients had higher, not lower, TP53 and TTN mutation rates.

statements.text: Contrary to expectation, mice lacking cGAS showed accelerated aging together with induction of inflammation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Unexpectedly, we found that cGAS knockout mice exhibit accelerated aging phenotype associated with induction of inflammation.
statements.note: The abstract calls the finding unexpected: cGAS knockout mice exhibited an accelerated aging phenotype with inflammation.

statements.text: STED microscopy localized cGAS condensates to the cytoplasm, away from H3K9me3-marked heterochromatin.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Stimulated emission depletion microscopy (STED) showed that cGAS forms nuclear condensates that co-localize with H3K9me3 heterochromatin marks
statements.note: STED showed cGAS forming nuclear condensates that co-localize with H3K9me3 heterochromatin marks.

statements.text: Blocking L1 reverse transcription rescues the accelerated aging of cGAS knockout mice.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We propose that loss of cGAS leads to loss of chromatin organization, de-repression of transposable elements and induction of inflammation resulting in accelerated aging.
statements.note: The causal chain from L1 de-repression to aging is proposed as a model; no rescue or intervention experiment is reported.

statements.text: L1 transposons in cells from cGAS knockout mice were more accessible and less DNA-methylated than in controls.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Cells from cGAS knockout mice showed increased chromatin accessibility and decreased DNA methylation on L1 transposons.
statements.note: Knockout cells showed increased chromatin accessibility and decreased DNA methylation on L1 transposons.

statements.text: Switching therapy at week 8 in patients with ctDNA progressive disease improves their survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The clinical utility of LB-RECIST to guide early treatment decisions is warranted through interventional trials.
statements.note: The study is observational; the conclusion explicitly defers clinical utility for guiding treatment decisions to future interventional trials.

statements.text: Patients with ctDNA partial response had a longer median overall survival than those with ctDNA progressive disease.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: patients with ctDNA partial response (CPR) and ctDNA progressive disease (CPD) had the worst clinical outcomes (mOS 16.4 and 25.5 months, and mPFS 12.7 and 11.9 months, respectively)
statements.note: Median OS was 16.4 months for CPR versus 25.5 months for CPD, so the partial-response group fared worse on OS.

statements.text: Complete ctDNA clearance at week 8 gave a median overall survival of 41.8 months, close to the 41.1 months seen with persistently undetectable ctDNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Complete clearance of ctDNA at week 8 (ctDNA complete response, CCR) demonstrated the best prognostic and predictive values [median (m) OS 41.8 months; mPFS not reached (NR)], similar to persistent undetectable ctDNA (ctDNA non-measurable disease, CND; mOS 41.1 months; mPFS NR).
statements.note: CCR (mOS 41.8 months) and CND (mOS 41.1 months) had similar, best-in-cohort outcomes, with median PFS not reached in both.

statements.text: Of the 130 enrolled patients, ctDNA results were available for 90 at week 8 of treatment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA results were available for 106 patients at baseline and 90 patients at week 8 of treatment.
statements.note: Results were available for 106 patients at baseline and 90 at week 8.

statements.text: The tumor had a mutational burden of 10 mut/Mb and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 20%, yet was microsatellite stable.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Molecular profiling of the resected tumor revealed a high TMB (10 mut/Mb), somatic mutations in MSH2 and ATM, and microsatellite stability (MSS). Immunohistochemistry demonstrated complete loss of MSH2/MSH6 expression, while PD-L1 expression was 20% (tumor proportion score).
statements.note: Profiling showed TMB 10 mut/Mb, PD-L1 TPS 20% and MSS, with MSH2 and ATM mutations and loss of MSH2/MSH6 expression.

statements.text: Pembrolizumab was started only after the patient had progressed on radioiodine and tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Based on these findings, pembrolizumab was initiated as first-line therapy.
statements.note: Pembrolizumab was given first-line; the patient was ineligible for radioiodine and TKIs because of a prior subarachnoid hemorrhage.

statements.text: First-line pembrolizumab produced a partial response that lasted seven months and was well tolerated.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The patient experienced clinical improvement and maintained a sustained partial response for seven months, with excellent tolerability.
statements.note: The patient maintained a sustained partial response for seven months with excellent tolerability.

statements.text: The response to pembrolizumab was attributable to the ATM mutation rather than to the loss of MSH2.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our findings underscore that alternative biomarkers, such as somatic mutations in DNA repair genes including MSH2 and ATM, may predict unexpected responses to immune checkpoint blockade
statements.note: MSH2 and ATM are named together as candidate biomarkers; the abstract does not attribute the response to one over the other.

statements.text: PFBS exposure cut total nitrogen removal efficiency by roughly half.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: PFBS exposure significantly deteriorated nitrogen removal, leading to a 10.16% reduction in total nitrogen removal efficiency.
statements.note: The reported reduction in total nitrogen removal efficiency was 10.16%, not about 50%.

statements.text: Nitrogen removal recovered to pre-exposure levels once PFBS was withdrawn from the system.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that PFBS exposure compromises anammox performance while simultaneously elevating antimicrobial resistance dissemination and pathogen-associated risks
statements.note: The abstract describes effects during PFBS exposure; no recovery phase after withdrawal is reported.

statements.text: Under PFBS exposure, the key anammox genes hzs and hdh each lost more than half of their relative abundance (54.65% and 57.32%).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The relative abundance of key anammox functional genes (hzs and hdh) decreased by 54.65% and 57.32%, respectively.
statements.note: hzs decreased by 54.65% and hdh by 57.32% in relative abundance.

statements.text: Alongside impaired nitrogen removal, PFBS exposure enriched both antibiotic resistance genes and mobile genetic elements in the community.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: PFBS facilitated the enrichment of ARG and mobile genetic elements (MGE), thereby increasing the potential for MGE-mediated ARG dissemination.
statements.note: PFBS facilitated enrichment of ARGs and MGEs, raising the potential for MGE-mediated ARG dissemination.

statements.text: LLM-based relevance filtering retained 50 on-topic papers per annual cohort, 100 in total, from more than 10,000 ranked articles per cohort.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Large language model (LLM)-based topical relevance filtering yielded 50 substantively on-topic papers per cohort (100 total).
statements.note: Over 10,000 OpenAlex articles per cohort were ranked, and LLM filtering yielded 50 on-topic papers per cohort (100 total).

statements.text: The drop in ctDNA-themed citation prominence reflects reduced funding for liquid biopsy research.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings indicate that early citation impact in cancer genomics is shifting toward integrative, spatially resolved, and heterogeneity-aware research
statements.note: The abstract reports the decline in liquid biopsy and ctDNA themes but offers no explanation for it.

statements.text: Large genomic resource and infrastructure papers, not single-disease mechanistic studies, topped the citation rankings in each cohort.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The most cited papers in both cohorts were large-scale genomic infrastructure resources rather than single-disease mechanistic studies.
statements.note: In both cohorts the most cited papers were large-scale genomic infrastructure resources.

statements.text: Liquid biopsy and ctDNA-related themes showed the largest increase in normalized frequency between the two cohorts.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: while liquid biopsy and ctDNA-related themes showed the largest declines
statements.note: Those themes showed the largest declines; the largest increases were for clonal evolution, single-cell and spatial omics, immune infiltration and CNV.

statements.text: The adverse FOLR2 association in LUSC arises because FOLR2+ macrophages suppress CD8 T-cell infiltration.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: TAM-associated prognostic effects reverse by tumor histology, supporting tumor-context–dependent macrophage polarization
statements.note: The study reports hazard ratios from survival models; no mechanism linking FOLR2 to T-cell infiltration is tested.

statements.text: In melanoma, higher FOLR2 expression independently predicted better survival, with a hazard ratio of 0.87 per standard deviation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In melanoma, higher FOLR2 (HR 0.87), TREM2 (HR 0.83), CD8A (HR 0.69), and CXCL9 (HR 0.67) independently predicted improved survival.
statements.note: FOLR2 (HR 0.87), TREM2, CD8A and CXCL9 all independently predicted improved survival in melanoma.

statements.text: Lung adenocarcinoma showed a strongly adverse effect of macrophage markers on survival.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: LUAD showed largely neutral macrophage effects.
statements.note: LUAD showed largely neutral macrophage effects; the adverse FOLR2 association was in LUSC.

statements.text: In lung squamous carcinoma, higher FOLR2 expression was associated with worse survival (HR 1.28).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In contrast, LUSC demonstrated an adverse association for FOLR2 (HR 1.28).
statements.note: LUSC demonstrated an adverse association for FOLR2 with HR 1.28.

statements.text: During dynamic monitoring, patients who stayed ctDNA-positive had a statistically significant shorter PFS than those who did not.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: patients who remained ctDNA+ during dynamic monitoring tended to have a shorter PFS than those who did not (3.90 months vs. 6.10 months, P = 0.135)
statements.note: The difference (3.90 vs 6.10 months) is described as a tendency with P = 0.135, i.e. not statistically significant.

statements.text: Patients classified ctDNA-positive by a 12-gene panel had a PFS of 5.16 months versus 9.05 months in ctDNA-negative patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients with ctDNA+, defined by 12 prognosis-relevant mutated genes, had a shorter progression-free survival (PFS) than ctDNA− patients (5.16 months vs. 9.05 months, P = 0.001)
statements.note: ctDNA+ versus ctDNA− PFS was 5.16 vs 9.05 months (P = 0.001).

statements.text: MATH score and ctDNA fraction correlated positively with treatment response, whereas CEA, CA125 and CA153 did not.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Positive correlations with treatment response were observed for MATH score (R = 0.24, P = 0.014) and ctDNA% (R = 0.3, P = 0.002), but not the CEA, CA125, or CA153.
statements.note: Correlations were R = 0.24 for MATH score and R = 0.3 for ctDNA%, with none for the three protein markers.

statements.text: These ctDNA findings apply equally to patients with early-stage, non-metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here, we investigated the value of ctDNA for predicting the prognosis and monitoring the treatment response in mTNBC patients.
statements.note: Only metastatic patients who had progressed after chemotherapy were enrolled; early-stage disease is not addressed.

statements.text: Human PBMCs showed the most significantly up-regulated TEs after SARS-CoV-2 infection (405), compared with 283 in monkeys and 206 in mice.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified 405, 283, and 206 significantly up-regulated transposable elements (TEs) in hPBMCs, monkeys, and mice, respectively.
statements.note: The counts of significantly up-regulated TEs were 405, 283 and 206 in hPBMCs, monkeys and mice, respectively.

statements.text: A set of 210 ERVs was up-regulated specifically in severe COVID-19, and their associated genes were enriched for immune response activation and histone modification.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we identified 210 ERVs specifically up-regulated in the severe COVID-19 group. The genes associated with these differentially expressed ERVs were enriched in processes such as immune response activation and histone modification.
statements.note: The 210 severe-specific ERVs were associated with genes enriched in immune response activation and histone modification.

statements.text: RT-qPCR validation was carried out in bone marrow-derived macrophages from mice infected with SARS-CoV-2.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: validation of our findings using RT-qPCR in Bone Marrow-Derived Macrophages (BMDMs) from mice infected by HSV-1 and VSV
statements.note: The RT-qPCR validation used BMDMs from mice infected with HSV-1 and VSV, not SARS-CoV-2.

statements.text: Up-regulation of HERV1_I-int and LTR7Y causally contributes to the hyperinflammation of severe COVID-19.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: HERV1_I-int: ERV1:LTR and LTR7Y: ERV1:LTR were highlighted as potential biomarkers for evaluating the severity of COVID-19.
statements.note: These two ERVs are proposed as severity biomarkers; no causal role in inflammation is tested.

statements.text: Of 62,773 transposon copies in the C. elegans VC2010 assembly, only 290 transposon-mobility genes retained a complete open reading frame.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Among the 62,773 copies of retro- and DNA transposons in the latest assembly of the C. elegans genome (VC2010), we found that the complete open reading frame structure was conserved in 290 transposon-mobility genes.
statements.note: The abstract gives 62,773 copies and 290 genes with a conserved complete ORF structure.

statements.text: Roughly half of the 290 intact transposon-mobility genes (145) also preserved the critical catalytic-core amino acids.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Critical amino acids at the catalytic core were conserved in only 145 of these 290 genes.
statements.note: Critical catalytic-core amino acids were conserved in only 145 of the 290 genes.

statements.text: Most of the 145 transposons with conserved catalytic residues are actively transposing in C. elegans populations.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: the comprehensive identification of potentially functional transposon-mobility genes in all transposon orders of a single species can provide a basis of molecular analysis
statements.note: The genes are called potentially functional on the basis of sequence; actual transposition activity is not measured.

statements.text: The majority of the 62,773 transposon copies in the genome remain autonomously mobile.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Thus, in contrast to the huge number of transposon copies in the genome, only a limited number of transposons are autonomously mobile.
statements.note: The abstract concludes that only a limited number of transposons are autonomously mobile, in contrast to the huge number of copies.

statements.text: PANGEM detects stage I cancers with the same sensitivity as late-stage cancers.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: PANGEM achieved the highest mean performance among evaluated methods, with an AUROC/AUPR of 0.997±0.003/1.000±0.000 for binary cancer detection
statements.note: Tumor stage is not mentioned anywhere in the abstract; performance is reported only overall and by tissue of origin.

statements.text: In the independent INSPIRE cohort, PANGEM flagged 72 of 78 cancer cases (92.3%) as cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In the independent INSPIRE cohort, 72 of 78 cancer cases (92.3%) exceeded the binary classification threshold
statements.note: 72 of 78 cancer cases exceeded the binary classification threshold in INSPIRE.

statements.text: Subnetwork analysis found a graph-connected module of 111 DMRs that was hypermethylated in cancer samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Subnetwork analysis further identified recurrent, graph-connected methylation patterns, including a 111-DMR subnetwork with increased methylation in cancer samples.
statements.note: A 111-DMR subnetwork with increased methylation in cancer samples was identified.

statements.text: PANGEM assigned the correct tissue of origin to 9 of 17 head and neck cancer cases, a lower accuracy than competing methods.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: PANGEM correctly classified 9 of 17 head and neck cancer cases (52.9%), the highest accuracy among evaluated methods
statements.note: The 9 of 17 (52.9%) result was the highest accuracy among the evaluated methods.

statements.text: In the external validation set of 149 participants, the locked model reached an AUC of 0.965 for separating gastric cancer from non-cancer controls.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the locked GastroAlert model exhibited robust and reproducible performance in the independent validation dataset, yielding an AUC of 0.965 (95% CI 0.940-0.989) for distinguishing gastric cancer patients from non-cancer controls
statements.note: The locked GastroAlert model yielded AUC 0.965 (95% CI 0.940-0.989) in the independent validation dataset of 149 participants.

statements.text: For early-stage gastric cancer the model's performance fell sharply, with an AUC below 0.80 in the validation dataset.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the model still maintained high diagnostic efficacy with an AUC of 0.921 (95% CI 0.862-0.980) in the discovery dataset and 0.948 (95% CI 0.910-0.985) in the validation dataset
statements.note: Early-stage AUC was 0.921 in discovery and 0.948 in validation.

statements.text: GastroAlert separated gastric cancer from benign gastric conditions as accurately as from healthy controls.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: a discovery dataset consisting of 136 participants, including 53 gastric cancer patients, 55 individuals with benign gastric conditions, and 28 healthy controls
statements.note: Benign and healthy participants were pooled as non-cancer controls; no separate performance against benign conditions is reported.

statements.text: Conventional protein biomarkers achieved AUCs of only 0.507 to 0.687 in the discovery dataset, far below GastroAlert's 0.950.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: GastroAlert achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.950 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.874-0.995], with observed AUCs for conventional protein biomarkers ranging from 0.507 to 0.687
statements.note: Cross-validated AUC was 0.950 for GastroAlert versus 0.507-0.687 for conventional protein biomarkers.

statements.text: Changes in ctDNA levels during treatment identified the patients who later relapsed.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: demonstrating its potential for minimal disease monitoring
statements.note: Only initial (pre-treatment) plasma was analyzed; monitoring is described as a potential, with no on-treatment or relapse data.

statements.text: In low-risk patients, the majority of mutations were shared between plasma and lymphoma DNA.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In patients with low-risk disease, 27% of mutations were shared in plasma and tumor; 65% and 8% were detected in DNA from lymphoma or plasma samples only.
statements.note: In low-risk disease only 27% of mutations were shared; 65% were found in lymphoma DNA only.

statements.text: Using a tumor-agnostic approach, 60% of somatic short variants in high-risk patients were detected in both plasma and lymphoma tissue.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In 10 patients with high-risk disease (risk groups R3 and R4), 60% of somatic short variants were detected in both plasma and lymphoma samples using a tumor-agnostic approach
statements.note: In the 10 high-risk patients, 60% of variants were shared, 26% were lymphoma-only and 14% plasma-only.

statements.text: With a tumor-informed approach, ctDNA was detected in 16 of 18 plasma samples, at fractions from 0.045% to 55%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In a tumor-informed approach, ctDNA was detectable in 16/18 plasma samples with a proportion of 0.045%-55%
statements.note: The tumor-informed analysis detected ctDNA in 16/18 samples with proportions of 0.045%-55%.

statements.text: Loss of chromosome arms 5q and 16q predicted worse prognosis across all 73 HCC patients, regardless of ctDNA status.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Among ctDNA-positive patients under systemic treatments, the loss of large genomic regions in 5q and 16q arms was associated with worse prognosis after multivariate analysis.
statements.note: The 5q/16q association was reported only among ctDNA-positive patients under systemic treatment.

statements.text: ctDNA detection before surgery also predicted recurrence in patients treated with resection.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Plasma samples were obtained from patients with HCC prior to surgery, locoregional or systemic therapy
statements.note: Samples were collected before surgery, locoregional or systemic therapy, but outcome results are reported only for the 31 systemically treated patients.

statements.text: ctDNA was detectable in 18 of 31 systemically treated patients, and detectable ctDNA meant a median overall survival of 13.96 months versus not reached.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA was detected in 18 out of 31 patients who received systemic treatment. Patients with detectable ctDNA showed significantly worse overall survival (median, 13.96 months vs not reached).
statements.note: 18/31 systemically treated patients had detectable ctDNA; median OS was 13.96 months versus not reached.

statements.text: After adjustment for clinical-pathologic features and systemic treatment type, ctDNA detection remained independently prognostic (HR 7.69, 95% CI 2.09-28.27).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA remained an independent predictor of prognosis after adjustment by clinical-pathologic features and type of systemic treatment (hazard ratio 7.69; 95%, CI 2.09-28.27).
statements.note: The adjusted hazard ratio for detectable ctDNA was 7.69 (95% CI 2.09-28.27).

statements.text: FGFR3-mutant UTUC patients in this cohort responded well to FGFR inhibitor therapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our research lays the foundation for understanding UTUC in China and designing precise diagnosis and treatment.
statements.note: FGFR3 alteration frequency (41.0%) is reported, but no treatment or response data are given.

statements.text: Somatic mutations were identified in 98.4% (120 of 122) of Chinese UTUC patients with the 520-gene targeted panel.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Somatic mutations were detected in 120/122 (98.4%) patients using this 520-gene panel sequencing.
statements.note: 120/122 patients (98.4%) had detectable somatic mutations.

statements.text: Tumors of the TP53/MDM2-mutant subtype had progression-free survival similar to that of other subtypes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: TP53/MDM2 -mutant subtype or triple-negative subtype had significantly worse progression-free survival than other subtypes.
statements.note: The TP53/MDM2-mutant and triple-negative subtypes had significantly worse progression-free survival than other subtypes.

statements.text: KMT2D alterations, at 48.4%, were slightly more frequent than TERT promoter alterations (46.7%) in this cohort.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The top-ranking altered genes in Chinese patients with UTUC were KMT2D (48.4%), TERT promoter (46.7%), FGFR3 (41.0%), and TP53 (37.7%).
statements.note: Top altered genes were KMT2D 48.4%, TERT promoter 46.7%, FGFR3 41.0% and TP53 37.7%.

statements.text: The cfDNA epigenomic test was modeled with a sensitivity of 97% and a specificity of 68%.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The cell-free DNA epigenomic test has a sensitivity of 68% and a specificity of 97%.
statements.note: The values are reversed: sensitivity 68%, specificity 97%.

statements.text: The modeled ICER for cfDNA testing in higher-risk NOD patients was $56,564, under the $100,000 willingness-to-pay threshold.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with an Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) of $56,564 at a Willingness to Pay (WTP) of $100,000
statements.note: The ICER was $56,564 at a WTP of $100,000, which the abstract calls robustly cost-effective.

statements.text: Imaging surveillance of higher-risk NOD patients was more cost-effective than cfDNA testing.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Additionally, imaging surveillance strategies were also evaluated.
statements.note: Imaging surveillance strategies were evaluated, but no result for them is reported in the abstract.

statements.text: With cfDNA testing, 32.4% of detected pancreatic cancers were predicted to be surgically resectable, versus 7.1% under no testing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with only 7.1% of cases eligible for surgery. In contrast, 71 PC cases are predicted to be detected with cfDNA testing. These cases would be more likely to be detected at an earlier, more treatable stage, with 32.4% eligible for surgical resection.
statements.note: 7.1% of cases were eligible for surgery without testing versus 32.4% with cfDNA testing in the 10,000-patient model cohort.
